newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate eases, baht firmer late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate eases, baht firmer late.

text.p: Rising liquidity, after the Thursday deadline for commercial banks to meet cash reserve requirements, cut the Thai overnight interbank rate down to a 11.00-11.50 percent range on late Thursday from 12.00 early in the morning, dealers said.
"Banks were more willing to lend excess funds in the afternoon after the reserve deadline passed. Liquidity would continue to rise tomorrow," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
Banks have to meet reserve requirements set by the Bank of Thailand on the seventh and 22nd of each month.
The baht firmed to 25.462-25.463 to the dollar near the close from 25.473-25.476 in the early morning in line with a weaker U.S. dollar abroad, dealers said.
"The market was quite active today. Most of the trade was in line with dollar movement in overseas markets," said one currency dealer.
The one-month dollar/baht swap premium rose to 8.75/9.75 satangs per dollar near the close from 8.50/9.50 in the morning.
The dollar/baht mid-rate was fixed at 25.46 against 25.50 on Wednesday.
